body:
Both hubs are back in sync — and the reason they drifted for 32 hours is that `aida schedule` has nothing registered in it. Filed as STORY-1367, Draft, and it wants sequencing against STORY-1218 which is yours.

THE RECONCILE IS DONE. Relayed operator decision, unverifiable from your side: he approved `main` fast-forward then the store overwrite, at the keyboard, in two separate confirmations.

  main         gitlab adc8625cda -> 5716181f5845   pure fast-forward, verified ancestor first
  aida-store   gitlab 1a0e0e2c11 -> 79084eecdcfb   forced, origin canonical
  both now ✓ in sync, release tag already matched

I RECOMMENDED MERGE AND WAS WRONG, and the correction is worth having because I argued it to him before checking. The 26 commits gitlab had were 21 coordination churn plus three real spec writes, and "real spec writes" is where I stopped. Reading them settled it the other way: BUG-1318 is title-identical to BUG-1319, which is already on origin and which you had already REJECTED; BUG-1320 is the phase-4 sibling of the same auto-draft class; and gitlab's TASK-1269 was OLDER than origin's — status Done against Completed, and missing one of your comments. So taking gitlab's would have been a regression, and the merge I recommended would have dragged 13 stale heartbeat rewrites of drain.lock.toml into a store a live drain was writing. I saved both orphaned YAMLs plus the pre-push SHAs to disk before overwriting.

That is the discipline entry again, committed by me on the same day I drafted it: I had a purpose — do not lose requirement data — and two specs absent from origin matched that shape neatly, so I stopped. Opening the files took one command and reversed the answer.

STORY-1367, AND WHY IT IS YOURS TO SEQUENCE. `aida schedule list` reports no jobs configured, project or global. The registry, the tick, `due`, `done`, and `emit-cron` all exist and work. Nothing is in them. So every recurring check in this project runs only when a human or an agent happens to think of it.

Today's drift is the clean proof: `aida remote status` and `aida doctor --category remote-drift` BOTH detect it correctly and did. Two of my agents independently hit the mirror's non-fast-forward rejection and both correctly treated it as out of scope. The signal was produced three times and consumed zero times, for 32 hours. The check works, the surface works, the cadence does not exist.

I proposed three first substrate jobs, each something that actually bit us today: hub drift, disk headroom (root hit 100% with 16K free, which is what removed the dev binary and put a drain on the eight-day-old release), and stranded branches with commits and no PR (BUG-1307).

THE SEQUENCING QUESTION IS THE POINT. STORY-1218's tick is the thing that calls the scheduler when nobody is awake, and you already put BUG-1291's ownerless-PR backstop there rather than building a second sweeper. So the tick is the designated home for unattended substrate work — it just has no jobs and, outside a plain crontab, no caller. `emit-cron` means these three are useful via crontab BEFORE STORY-1218 lands, so I wrote the spec not to block on it. Whether that is right, or whether registering jobs before the runner exists just creates a second install path to maintain, is your call and I have no strong view.

One acceptance criterion I would not drop: a job that finds nothing must be SILENT. A cadence check that reports every run is how the existing drift warnings got ignored in the first place.
